name: Wab
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.source_named: Glottolog wabb1237 lists only survey wordlists (Carter et al. 2012 Mur Village survey, Claassen & McElhanon 1970); no grammar/phonology of Wab exists.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.1 languoid page and langdoc listing for wabb1237; Wikipedia 'Yote language'; the Internet Archive 2015 snapshot of sil.org resource listing for [wab]
sources.note: Glottolog lists no grammar/phonology/sketch for Wab; the SIL listing showed only the 2012 survey; Wikipedia stub cites only Ethnologue.

sources.citation: Carter, John, Katie Carter, John Grummitt, Bonnie MacKenzie & Janell Masters. 2012. A Sociolinguistic Survey of the Mur Village Vernaculars. SIL Electronic Survey Reports 2012-043. Dallas: SIL International. 70 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress. Wab appears only as a 40-item wordlist elicited by Peter Lincoln in 1976 (Appendix A, Table 9, pp. 39, 49) compared lexically with Dawang; Appendix B.3 (pp. 45-46) gives a Dawang phone chart, possessive suffixes and word order, with no mention of stress. The report states 'no survey has been done of Wab' (p. 9).

sources.citation: Ross, Malcolm D. 1988. Proto Oceanic and the Austronesian languages of western Melanesia. Pacific Linguistics C-98. Canberra: ANU.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request); access check: open copy online; also in print at Harvard (Widener Library (offsite storage), call number PL6201.R67 1988) (also lendable online at archive.org)
sources.harvard_location: Widener Library (offsite storage), call number PL6201 .R67 1988
sources.note: No stress statement for Wab or any Bel language. Wab forms (from Lincoln 1976e mimeo wordlists, data-sources appendix) enter the Bel-family reconstructions and consonant-correspondence tables (pp. 160-173 and tables following); the only 'unstressed vowel' remarks are about Hote/Buang and Schouten languages.

sources.citation: Z'graggen, John A. 1976. Austronesian languages: Madang Province. In S. A. Wurm (ed.), New Guinea area languages and language study, vol. 2, 285-299. Pacific Linguistics C-39. Canberra: ANU.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Places Wab (Som) in an 'Astrolaban Sub-Family' with Mindiri and Biliau and gives lexical comparison tables; no phonological description.

sources.citation: Z'graggen, John A. 1975. The languages of the Madang District, Papua New Guinea. Pacific Linguistics B-41. Canberra: ANU. 156 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Classification, village census (Wab = X12 'Som', 142 speakers) and lexicostatistics; no phonology.

sources.citation: Claassen, Oren R. & Kenneth A. McElhanon. 1970. Languages of the Finisterre Range - New Guinea. Papers in New Guinea Linguistics 11, 45-78. Pacific Linguistics A-23. Canberra: ANU.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Wab is mentioned only as a village name near Saidor; no Wab language data.

sources.citation: SIL PNG. 2001. Yote (Wab, Som) Alphabet Development Worksheet. 15 pp. SIL Language & Culture Archives entry 70479 (draft, AusAID-sponsored, compiled with eight named Yote speakers).
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: The only item on record produced from first-hand work with Wab speakers that is catalogued as 'language description' and 'orthography'; SIL PNG alphabet-development worksheets normally cover syllable structure and suprasegmentals, so it is the likeliest place a stress note exists. Held by SIL PNG archives; request via 'Contact the Archives'.

sources.citation: SIL PNG. 2001. Yote Awed: Trial Spelling Guide for the Yote Language. 17 pp. Wab Village, Raikos District, Saidor. SIL Language & Culture Archives entry 70512.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Companion trial spelling guide from the same 2001 workshop; a spelling guide may state whether stress is written and where it falls.

sources.citation: Lincoln, Peter C. 1976. Rai Coast Austronesian language survey data, in two parts. Mimeo (Ross 1988 'Lincoln 1976e').

sources.note: The primary Wab wordlist data (source of Ross 1988 and of the 40-item list in Carter et al. 2012); Carter et al. note it used a different transcription technique, which might mark stress. Unpublished mimeo; possibly in UPNG or ANU (Ross) files.
